review_notes: I read all of Constants.lean (lines 1–90). I also read the constant definitions in AboveTwoStatements.lean (aboveUniformConstant through aboveGamma) and every use of these lemmas in Proofs/. The file has no simp attributes. Every declaration is a positivity or inequality fact with hypothesis `2 < p`, or a single product identity. Downstream code uses them as explicit terms, for example `Stage4AboveTwo.hpConstant_pos hp` passed to `div_pos`, or `have hB := ...`. None of the uses relies on simp or unfolds these definitions with simp. The one equation, `errorPower_mul_budgetExponent`, is consumed with `rw` in WeightBalance.lean (`rw [mul_comm, errorPower_mul_budgetExponent hp]`). It carries the hypothesis `2 < p`, and the `mul_comm` step is a local detail. So making it a simp lemma is not clearly justified, and I found no competing rule, loop, unwanted expansion or rewrite in a bad direction. The one nearby weakness is that WeightBalance.lean re-proves positivity of `aboveGamma` inline instead of reusing `gamma_pos`. That is a duplication issue, not a simp-interface one, so I did not report it. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out interactions I did not read.
